title: 24th sitting of the 20th Majlis
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with 56 members present and none on official travel. Most of the part was the question session for Health Minister Dr. Abdulla Khalil, with members from many islands asking when health centres and hospitals in their constituencies will be built or upgraded; he mostly answered that designs, funding and approvals are still being worked through. After a break from 10:29 to 11:01, the floor moved to the first debate on the Insurance Bill sponsored by Mahibadhoo MP Ahmed Thariq, where the first four speakers backed it and the fifth was just starting when this part ends. The second half of the debate on the Insurance Bill continued in the chamber. Three members spoke: one finishing a speech that began earlier, and two more who supported the bill while asking for committee-stage changes on points such as application fees, fines, Dhivehi-language contracts and local ownership. The chair noted that several committees were meeting at the same time, which explained the thin attendance, then closed the debate and adjourned until 9:00 on Wednesday 7 August 2024.

items.title: Question to Health Minister Dr. Abdulla Khalil from Velidhoo MP Mohamed Abbas on the Lhohi health centre building
items.outcome: answered; 13 other members asked follow-ups on hospitals, ambulances, dialysis and doctors

items.title: Initial debate on the Insurance Bill (submitted by the government)
items.outcome: debated; chair closed the debate, bill proceeds to committee stage

speakers.name: Dr. Abdulla Khalil
positions: As Health Minister, said many past hospital and health centre plans were office-style designs without funding, and are being redesigned around services.
Said projects such as Foddhoo, Vilufushi and Hanimaadhoo are delayed by funding, Kuwait Fund signing and contractor payment arrears.
Said doctor turnover is high and more doctors, CT scans and dialysis are being rolled out to atoll hospitals over the year.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked what has been done and when work will start on the Foddhoo health centre, which has no health centre.
Asked about progress on the Lhohi health centre extension.
Asked when Velidhoo hospital works start and when N. atoll hospital will offer CT scans.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked why the Kendhoo 24-hour health centre is not open and about medicine shortages and missing dialysis in the atoll.
Asked how Kihaadhoo's unregistered ambulance can start working, when dialysis will be available, and about pay for health support staff.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked how many pharmacies lack medicine and about progress on the Addu tertiary hospital.
Raised a point of order, which the chair did not accept, saying the minister's claim of no funds was unfair after eight months.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked about the previous government's agreement for a tertiary hospital in Thinadhoo.
Raised a point of order, which the chair did not accept, asking whether a signed agreement exists.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked when work starts on the Neykurendhoo and Kurinbi health centres.
Asked whether this government has built any health centre, why cancers are rising, and its plan to strengthen public health.

speakers.name: Dr. Anara Naeem
positions: Asked when 24-hour health centre service will be arranged for the islands in her constituency, which host many tourists.
In the Insurance Bill debate, supported it and asked the committee to address overlap between Aasandha and other health insurance, and to consider takaful.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Asked when budgeted health centres in three islands will start, when posts and permits will be approved, and whether answers differ between members.
Called the bill thorough but raised points for committee: application fees not refundable if a licence is refused, and a large capital deposit.
Asked for takaful rules and for majority Maldivian staff and shares over time.
Questioned whether a fine of about MVR 100,000 a day for withholding information is proportionate.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Thanked the minister for the IV stand, asked how Hoarafushi hospital works can be sped up, and whether a lift can replace the ramp.
Called the bill important for a growing service industry and welcomed international best practice.
Wants motor and third-party insurance agreements available in Dhivehi, and asked whether the state gets GST/tax from resorts insured abroad.
Urged that health, aviation and takaful insurance be covered, and that the committee consult insurers and stakeholders.

speakers.name: Mohamed Niushad
positions: Asked when work on the decayed Keyodhoo health centre will start, given a small budget allocation.
Raised a point of order, which the chair did not accept as one.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Asked about the progress of the Rathafandhoo health centre announced in March and the pharmacy relocation at Faresmaathodaa.

speakers.name: Hassan Waheed
positions: Asked when work on the planned Thaa Vilufushi hospital will start.

speakers.name: Ahmed Zahir
positions: Asked when work starts on the Maduvvari health facility and the planned Meedhoo hospital.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said Feydhoo health centre serves many people but lacks beds and facilities, and asked for solutions and any planned project.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Said no island in his constituency has a specialist doctor, especially for women, and asked about the plan and about missing X-ray and scanning.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked whether an ambulance can be stationed at Maradhoo health centre, since AEH ambulances take about 20-30 minutes.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked for an update on health facilities for Maafaru airport and the N. atoll hospital building.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Asked when work on Hanimaadhoo hospital will begin, noting the government said it would start this year.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked when the planned hospital in his area will start and how the work is progressing.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when the long-stalled Kelaa health building will finish and when the unusable Filladhoo office building will be connected to water.

speakers.name: Faruhath Mohamed
positions: Asked when the Kulhudhuffushi regional hospital extension and a full emergency room will be built.

speakers.name: Adam Shafeeq
positions: Asked when work starts on the Makunudhoo building, when Kumundhoo goes 24-hour, and whether more doctors can be sent to three islands.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Asked when work starts on the regional hospital building and for an update on the mental hospital.

speakers.name: Ahmed Thariq
positions: Presented the government's Insurance Bill, which sets a legal framework, licensing and MMA oversight for insurers and intermediaries.
Suggested committee consider requiring a share of premiums to be kept in the Maldives and hearing industry concerns.

speakers.name: Munthazim Ibrahim
positions: Supported the bill, noting it was parked in the 19th Majlis, and said a law will ease regulation, claims and investor confidence.

speakers.name: Abdulla Rifau
positions: Supported the bill, said unpaid claims such as the Aliddhoo resort fire show the need, and flagged unclear clauses for committee.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Opened by calling the Insurance Bill important; his remarks continue into part 2.
Continued a speech begun in part 1: supports the bill in full, praising its board structure, the CEO requirement and the rule that large shareholdings need regulator approval.

decisions: The chair did not accept the points of order raised by the South Hithadhoo, North Thinadhoo and Keyodhoo members as valid points of order.
Four hours were allotted to the preliminary debate on the Insurance Bill, split among parties and unaffiliated members.
The sitting took a break from 10:29 to 11:01 and then resumed with the Insurance Bill debate.
The chair closed the initial debate on the Insurance Bill after the members' speeches.
The chair announced the next sitting for 9:00 on Wednesday 7 August 2024.
The chair informed members that several committees were meeting during the sitting.
